evidence.note: Creates a task ledger explicitly partitioned by subsystem (Cargo/build+size, schema/seed, markdown/Rouge, routes/middleware/templates/feeds, job queue, 500-trace replay parity) — a structured done-vs-remaining map for the port.

TaskUpdate status transitions (completed/in_progress) spread across the whole horizon show the agent maintaining and advancing the subsystem checklist as pieces pass, not declaring done from the last thing touched.

Built a trace-replay/differential harness and re-ran it after making fixes ('Replay traces again', 'Re-run HTML diff after fixes', 'Final 500-trace replay') — harness-backed coverage checks that guard against regression.

When the excerpt-comparison verification stalled/was too slow, agent checked progress, read output, then changed tactic (fast batched comparison, set TMPDIR, cleaned disk) — recognizing a stuck loop and reallocating, though this concerned test tooling rather than a parity mismatch.
Final coverage sweep before completion: full replay, cross-runtime job test, concurrency/latency, forbidden-crate/size check — confirming parity across subsystems rather than a single endpoint.

reasoning: The agent maintains a subsystem-mapped task ledger updated across the full horizon and backs it with a differential replay harness that it re-runs after fixes and in a final sweep, clearing the 'running checklist' anchor (5). It shows some stuck-detection and tactic change (240-256) and end-of-run regression guarding, pushing toward 8, but the ledger is coarse (6 tasks, not explicit per-subsystem passing/failing/not-yet-attempted), there is no clear instance of catching a regression in a previously-passing area, and no coverage-driven prioritization of the highest-value remaining gaps. That places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.
